items.exemplar:
A. The United States asserted itself by annexing Hawaii in 1898 after American planters overthrew Queen Liliuokalani, extending American sovereignty into the Pacific.

B. Roosevelt's Corollary (1904) and the Panama Canal (completed 1914) announced an American police power in the Caribbean and a two-ocean navy anchored by the canal.

C. Americans rejected empire through the Anti-Imperialist League: figures like Mark Twain and Andrew Carnegie denounced the Philippine war as a betrayal of republican principles.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE example of the United States asserting itself as a world power in the period 1890–1913.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that assertion in the same period.
C. Briefly explain ONE example of Americans rejecting America's assertion as a world power.
items.stimulus:
"I left these shores a red-hot imperialist. I wanted the American eagle to go screaming into the Pacific... But I have thought some more, since then, and I have seen that we do not intend to free, but to subjugate the people of the Philippines."
—Mark Twain, 1900 (abridged)
